config.question: Does the classic signed-square-root + per-row L2 normalisation lift the sealed f6144 codes at matched cost?

registration_notes.N99.1: C1 is a FREE fit on the sealed M117 memmaps (never re-encoded). The transform is the Fisher-vector post-processing: y = sign(x)|x|^p then per-row L2 normalise.
registration_notes.N99.2: Registered anchor: p=1.0 is the identity up to a positive per-row scale, and argmax is invariant to positive row scaling, so the p=1.0 ridge read MUST reproduce the sealed Q(6144, 138000) = 0.22487 within 0.002. This pins the transform arithmetic.
registration_notes.N99.3: Reads per cell: ridge read (penalty ladder), trained-head read (SGD linear head, the co-adaptation control), and the closed-form joint grid (p x penalty).
registration_notes.N99.4: Gate: the best (p, penalty) ridge read at the 138k level must beat 0.22487 + 0.005, else C1 is a scoped negative. The 207k level (sealed ext600 memmap, 69,000 rows reused) is reported alongside.
registration_notes.N99.5: The full-data frontier gate (Q(6144, 409832) = 0.261362) is DEFERRED to the escalation cell: the full-data codes were never cached by M141 and need a fresh ~2h encode; only winners of this free screen are escalated.
registration_notes.N99.6: Encode cells C2 (spatial-pyramid 1x1+2x2+4x4, 21 bins), C3 (multi-scale patches 3/5/7 with per-scale whiteners) and C4 (SPM + power-norm) are registered in this config's deferred_cells and NOT dispatched tonight.
registration_notes.N99.7: Smoke runs declare _smoke_note and MUST refuse the sealed output directory.
